task.description:
Test design gate for REQ-070 (WF-02 step 5b), FIRST pass (maximum three passes: first and two repeats; a third FAIL means ORCH stops and asks the owner). You work in a copy; you change only your handoff. No commits, no git checkout/reset/stash/clean (also not in scratch copies). 16 GB RAM computer: single commands, one test run at a time, close what you start; the owner's servers on ports 4782 and 4790 must not be touched.
Read: the design docs/design/REQ-070-demo-tenants-v3.md (8.1 criterion table, 8.2 the 21 tests, 8.3 literals, section 12 mutants), the block REQ-070 in docs/requirements.yaml (seven criteria; criterion 2 as amended with SEP), decisions 0086, the result of step 08 (self_check table), the new test tools/test/picker-demo-v3.test.js and the data tools/src/picker/demo-tenants-v3/, demo-answers-v3/.
Check yourself, do not trust the report:
(1) Every one of the seven criteria has a runnable test that fails when the criterion is broken (criterion 5, the independent reader, is a step of the acceptance, not a test: say so and check the test side of the counts it names; the run-relative git diff of criterion 6 and the test( count loop of criterion 7 are commands run by RELEASE-VALIDATOR: run them yourself once and report); nothing is skipped, todo, only or conditional.
(2) Oracles are independent of the code: own contrast function and HSL function with literal sheets, literal tables, the sample loaded with a substituted window and compared by the path map; no checked function is imported to compute an expected value (imports only to call them); the literals of 8.3 equal the ones measured on a clean copy of the tag base/DEMO070-20261027-01 (reproduce the hashes of the six old questionnaires and the old data files yourself).
(3) Independence: run the new test file alone twice, and once in a different position (together with the picker-server and picker-look test files in reverse order); no fixed port; no leftover temporary folders; no clock.
(4) Mutants: apply yourself, one at a time on a scratch copy (restore after each; sequential), every fifth mutant of section 12 (MU5, MU10, MU15, MU20, MU25, MU30) plus MU2, MU19, MU29, and at least EIGHT mutants of your own, not in the design list and not the author's four (OM1, OM3-OM5): aim at the data and at the tests' blind spots — for example swap two desks' staff names between the files, change a kk phrase of a shared word, change a `price_text` of one solution to the other tenant's wording, change `top` or `result` settings, change `half` to contain answers 2 and 3 instead of 1 and 2, drop `consent_text` in one language, change a unit of the number question, change a chip value to a non-integer, turn a `required` into false, remove the `show_if`-free rule by adding a `show_if`, change a `figure` id to one outside the twelve, make the intro number 4 only in kk of agency. Every non-equivalent mutant must make at least one test red; report equivalent mutants with a reason.
(5) Run `cd tools && npm run check` once at the end in the live tree: green (2065 tests expected), the sha256 of the sorted per-file sha256 list of tools/src (data folders included) equal at start and end.
Verdict PASS or FAIL with findings (severity, file, line, fix). Only a surviving non-equivalent mutant on a stated criterion, a missing criterion test or a real defect makes FAIL; Low findings go to the follow-up list. In your handoff text never list project names or machine paths (say "the traces list").

findings.what: DT-3a pins only the keys of half (the first two question ids). The values of half are checked only as valid options or numbers. Design D6 says half = the answers of leader to the first two questions; a half that holds another valid option (my mutant: stock half.sites = few instead of one) is green. No criterion states the values (criterion 3: half answers exactly the first two questions; what REQ-072 does with it is REQ-072's), so this is a gap of the design's own statement, not of a criterion.
findings.fix: In DT-3a add for each tenant: assert.deepEqual(answers.half, Object.fromEntries(ids.slice(0, 2).map((k) => [k, answers.leader[k]]))), or literals of the two values; REQ-072 can then rely on it.

findings.what: The wording of the texts the sample does not hold (solution summary, includes, needs_from_you, next_steps, not_suitable_when, rule and hypothesis texts, no_match_text, consent_text, operator_name, privacy_contact) is pinned only by shape, by the lists lengths, by equal numbers, by no Cyrillic in en, by being non-empty and by not being shared with the other file. Reordering the includes list of a solution (my mutant V37) is green. This is by design (the wording belongs to the executor and the meaning to the reader of criterion 5, D1), so it is recorded, not a defect.
findings.fix: None needed now. If a later requirement relies on the order of includes or on a name, pin that single value then.
